title: Surjectivity descends to a stage of an algebraic-space inverse system
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Local finite presentation and local finite type are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(B_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces with affine transitions and limit $B$, and choose $i_0\in I$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism over $B_{i_0}$ with $X_0,Y_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $i\geq i_0$ put $X_i=X_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$ and let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$; let $f:X\to Y$ be its base change to $B$. If $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation and $|f|$ is surjective, then there is $j\geq i_0$ such that $|f_i|$ is surjective for every $i\geq j$. No surjectivity of the transition morphisms $B_j\to B_i$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07SN (lemma-descend-surjective) in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property); persistence under later base change.

proof.text: Choose an affine scheme $V_0$ with a surjective etale map $V_0\to Y_0$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. The affine scheme $V_0$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $W_0=X_0\times_{Y_0}V_0$ is qcqs by [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product]. Choose an affine scheme $U_0$ with a surjective etale map $U_0\to W_0$ using the same atlas lemma. The scheme morphism $h_0:U_0\to V_0$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], applied to $f_0$ and these two charts. Thus $U_0,V_0$ are qcqs schemes and $h_0$ has exactly the local finite presentation needed for scheme descent.

source.place: Tag 07SN (lemma-descend-surjective), proof in Situation 084W; use the affine target-chart system as the scheme base system.

proof.text: On the directed tail $i\geq i_0$, set $V_i=V_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$ and $U_i=U_0\times_{B_{i_0}}B_i$, and similarly $V,U$ over $B$. The maps $B_i\to B_{i_0}$ are affine; the limit projection is affine by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]. Hence $U_i,V_i,U,V$ are affine schemes, and the transition maps are affine, by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. The base-change identity for limits in [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] identifies $U=\varprojlim U_i$ and $V=\varprojlim V_i$. The sheaf limit universal property, restricted to scheme tests, is also the scheme limit universal property. Pullback associativity identifies $U_i$ with $U_0\times_{V_0}V_i$ and $U$ with $U_0\times_{V_0}V$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $V_i\to Y_i$ and $U_i\to X_i\times_{Y_i}V_i$ are surjective etale, and the analogous statements hold over $B$. These are precisely base changes of the chosen two charts.

source.place: Tag 07SN (lemma-descend-surjective), proof in Situation 084W; use the affine target-chart system as the scheme base system.

proof.text: Surjectivity of $|f|$ implies surjectivity of $|X\times_YV|\to|V|$ by the point-image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Since $U\to X\times_YV$ is surjective, the composite $h:U\to V$ is surjective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] with scheme bases $S_i=V_i$, distinguished stage $i_0$, stage source $U_0$, stage target $V_0$, and morphism $h_0$. Here $V_{i_0}\cong V_0$; every base is affine, $U_0,V_0$ are qcqs, the transitions are affine, the scheme limit is $V$, and $h_0$ is locally of finite presentation by step 1. This gives $j\geq i_0$ for which $h_j:U_j\to V_j$ is surjective. In particular this application does not assume that the original $B_i$ are schemes.

source.place: Tag 07SN (lemma-descend-surjective), proof in Situation 084W; use the affine target-chart system as the scheme base system.

proof.text: For each point $y\in|Y_j|$, choose a preimage $v\in|V_j|$ and then a preimage $u\in|U_j|$ under $h_j$. The image of $u$ in $|X_j|$ maps to $y$, by commutativity of the chart square. Thus $|f_j|$ is surjective. For every $i\geq j$, pullback associativity identifies $f_i$ with the base change of $f_j$ along $Y_i\to Y_j$. The point-image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $\operatorname{im}|f_i|=|Y_i|$, so all these maps are surjective. No transition map has been assumed surjective.

The split follows that proof one step for one and leaves the statement unchanged; it adds no new nodes. Step 1: the atlas lemma (03H6) needs only |Y_0| quasi-compact, which holds. 073B(3) applies with X_0, V_0 and Y_0 all qcqs, so W_0 is qcqs. The chart test (0410) holds for every chart pair and gives h_0 lfp. Step 2: by pullback pasting, U_i = U_0 x_{V_0} V_i. Affine base change and the affine limit projection (limits node) make U_i, V_i, U, V affine schemes. The base-change limit clause gives V = lim V_i and U = lim U_i. The stage-0 charts base-change to surjective étale charts by the one-member family clause of 02X2/041F. Step 3: the point-image formula gives |X x_Y V| -> |V| surjective, and the representable-surjectivity clause makes h scheme-surjective. 07RR (lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective) is then applied with base system S_i = V_i, X_0 = U_0, Y_0 = V_0. All its hypotheses hold, and its base changes are exactly U_i -> V_i, so the B_i need not be schemes. Step 4 is marked elementary. It needs |T| -> |h_T| surjective for a scheme T, which is a two-line consequence of the definitions in def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes, so the marking is acceptable. It then chases preimages and gets persistence for i >= j from the image formula. Small cases checked: Y_0 empty, B empty with nonempty stages, and a constant system. The delivery adds no cycle and duplicates nothing. I accept the four tool_uses (affine qcqs, 07RR, a1 point calculus, trf fibre products): each is a generic input the 07SN route needs.
